summary:
Solids retention time, or sludge age, is how long a bacterium stays in the system, and it decides which organisms survive there. It returns solids inventory, solids retention time and wasting rate for the target SRT, and the panel shows all of them at once.

This calculator returns SRT from the tank inventory and the daily sludge wasting, plus the wasting rate needed to hit a target age. Every result is derived from the boxes you fill in, so changing one input updates the whole panel at once. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: The formula behind the Solids Retention Time (SRT)
sections.html:
SRT = (V × MLSS) ÷ (Q_w × MLSS_w + Q_e × TSS_e), all masses in the same units

The symbols in the formula
SymbolWhat it stands forUnit
Vaeration tank volumem³
Q_wwaste sludge flowm³/day
MLSS_wwasted sludge concentrationmg/L
Q_eeffluent flowm³/day

sections.title: How do I use the Solids Retention Time (SRT)?
sections.html:
The form asks only for what the formula needs — nothing is optional decoration.

  1. Enter the values you already have. Every box accepts a decimal point and a minus sign; thousands separators are ignored.
  2. The grey boxes are results: they are worked out from your inputs and cannot be typed into.
  3. Press Calculate. The results fill in together, and from then on they follow every edit you make — there is no page to reload and nothing to submit.

sections.title: A worked example
sections.html:
Take the default values the page opens with: aeration tank volume of 750 m³, mlss of 3,000 mg/L, waste sludge flow of 25 m³/day, waste sludge mlss of 8,000 mg/L, effluent flow of 500 m³/day, effluent suspended solids of 15 mg/L, target srt of 15 days.

Substituting them into the formula gives solids inventory of 2,250 kg, solids retention time of 10.84 days, wasting rate for the target srt of 17.81 m³/day.

The arithmetic is the page's own: change one box and the result moves by the amount the formula implies, which is the quickest way to convince yourself the tool is honest.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
A raw figure only means something next to the bands it is normally judged against. Here is the scale that goes with this one:

How to read the result
ResultBandWhat it means
2 – 4 daysHigh ratefast growth, poor nitrification
5 – 10 daysConventionalBOD removal, partial nitrification
10 – 20 daysNitrifyingstable ammonia removal
above 25 daysExtended aerationsludge stabilisation, low yield

  • SRT, not hydraulic retention time, controls the biology: a plant can have a four-hour hydraulic pass and a fifteen-day sludge age at the same time.

  • Nitrifying bacteria grow slowly, so a plant designed for ammonia removal needs an SRT of at least 8–10 days at 15 °C and more when colder.

  • Solids lost over the weir count. On a plant with poor clarification, effluent TSS can be the dominant term in the denominator.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
The arithmetic is simple; the inputs are where things go wrong. The usual culprits:

  • Quoting hydraulic retention time when asked about sludge age.
  • Ignoring effluent suspended solids, which quietly shorten the SRT.
  • Wasting from the return line without using the return concentration in the calculation.

faq.q: How long should sludge be kept in an activated-sludge plant?
faq.a: 5–10 days for BOD removal, 10–20 for nitrification, 25 and above for stabilisation.
Yes — surplus sludge falls roughly as 1/SRT, which is why long ages produce less waste sludge.

faq.q: What does the Solids Retention Time (SRT) actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns solids inventory, solids retention time and wasting rate for the target SRT. Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.

faq.q: Can I use it with the numbers straight from a datasheet?
faq.a: Yes. Every box states its unit, and nothing is converted behind your back, so a figure copied from a datasheet, a kit insert or a protocol goes in as printed.
